author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.56.0. The tiering comments still hold: grounded tests come from resolved edges, and the name-hit tier is explicitly labelled a guess. Its short-name set is built through refs.short_of now, so a same-named def's #N suffix cannot leak into a name match and quietly stop matching the test that mentions it.

author: cli
text:
Re-read at the unparsed-file fix. Every earlier claim holds - still a pure read at the query layer, still computed against the WORKING TREE.

NEW: `unparsed` rides on BOTH exits, and the EARLY one is the one that matters. A file nobody could parse produces no entities, so when it is the only change, changed_ids is empty and the function returns through the early exit - which is precisely where the old code said 'no entity-level changes detected'. Adding the field to the main return only would have left the hole exactly where it was.

author: agent
text:
Re-read at 0.63.0. Every earlier claim holds - still a pure read at the query layer, still computed against the WORKING TREE, and `unparsed` still rides on BOTH exits with the early one being the one that mattered.

WHAT CHANGED: 65 lines came out. The reverse-reachability walk and the two-tier test selection are now verify.tests_reaching, called from here. Behaviour is identical; the copy is not.

WHY IT MOVED RATHER THAN BEING DUPLICATED. The same walk answers a second question - "what covers this entity BEFORE I touch it" - which primitives.covering_tests now asks. Writing it twice is the exact shape behind every drifted rule this project has recorded: the ring rule hand-rolled in the queue, the .coord exclusion missed by a second commit count, one metadata import written four ways, the confirm-suppression rule in three places before rot_is_answered was lifted out. The lesson each time was to extract BEFORE the second copy exists, not after, and this is the first time that has actually been done in that order.

A test pins it: primitives.covering_tests is parsed by AST and must contain a call to tests_reaching and must NOT mention deque, is_test_entity or _pytest_node. Reimplementing the walk fails the suite rather than merely being frowned upon.
